question: What are the trunks made of?
html:
Our trunks are made from recycled plastic bottles, with about 11 bottles going into each pair (Fair Harbor public filings). By the end of 2021, that came to about 26 million bottles recycled into our products (Fair Harbor public filings).

What our records confirm

  • Material source: recycled plastic bottles.
  • Bottles per trunk: about 11.
  • Cumulative bottles through 2021: about 26 million.
  • Brand role: recycled material is central to our shift from a swim brand to a year-round, sustainable lifestyle brand (Fair Harbor growth plan).

What our records don't cover

Our current sources do not answer these questions:

  • Fibre blend: the exact percentages of each fibre in the shell fabric.
  • Liner: what the liner is made of.
  • Consistency across styles: whether every trunk style uses the same material.
  • Non-swim lines: whether golf, kids, collegiate and B2B custom use recycled fabric.
  • Recent totals: the bottle count after 2021.

Current product spec sheets and supplier fabric certificates would answer these questions. Until we have them, we won't quote a blend or a newer total.

Why non-swim lines matter

Most of our live range is now non-swim. A materials answer that covers only trunks leaves a gap for most products a shopper might be looking at.

The recycled-bottle story is the clearest proof point behind the year-round lifestyle thesis. It also gives commissioned reps a simple pitch as we take the business from about 250 to about 520 specialty doors over 36 months.

Next actions

  1. Publish trunk compositions: collect current fabric spec sheets for every live trunk style and add the composition to each product page.
  2. Update the bottle count: get post-2021 bottle totals from fabric suppliers so the public figure is current.
  3. Check non-swim materials: confirm which golf, kids, collegiate and B2B custom products use recycled materials, and record the answer by product line.
  4. Brief the CX agents: load the verified materials data into the fit and CX agents' knowledge base in HarborOS so they answer this question consistently.
